output.scope_note: The paper is about Na3PS4, a sodium solid-state ion conductor, and reports measured room-temperature ionic conductivities for cubic, tetragonal and amorphous phases.

records.synthesis_method: ball milling of amorphous Na3PS4 followed by annealing
records.evidence_quote: In this study, the conductivity of the cubic Na3PS4 specimen showed a room-temperature conductivity of 1.3×10−4 S cm−1, which was higher than that of tetragonal Na3PS4 (1.9×10−5 S cm−1).
records.notes: Cubic phase obtained by heating amorphous Na3PS4 at 240 °C (Materials and Methods); annealing temperature is not a sintering temperature so the sintering field is null.

records.synthesis_method: ball milling of amorphous Na3PS4 followed by annealing
records.evidence_quote: In this study, the conductivity of the cubic Na3PS4 specimen showed a room-temperature conductivity of 1.3×10−4 S cm−1, which was higher than that of tetragonal Na3PS4 (1.9×10−5 S cm−1).
records.notes: Value given in the comparison sentence; the measurement temperature is not explicitly stated for this value (the sentence refers to room-temperature conductivity for the cubic specimen). Tetragonal phase obtained by heating amorphous Na3PS4 at 480 °C per Materials and Methods.

records.evidence_quote: The amorphous phase itself cannot increase the conductivity because the amorphous Na3PS4 prepared by ball-milling in this study has a lower conductivity of 4.1×10−6 S cm−1 than cubic and tetragonal Na3PS4 specimens.
records.notes: Measurement temperature not stated in the quoted sentence.
